content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Belinda Fuentes (E039), requesting admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment: full-time Analyst, requested admin to Payroll; admin only if role owns system (Payroll Specialist), so maximum is write. Recommend write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Comment: contractor with basic training, max read; admin never allowed. Recommend read. Conflicts with HR note; going with Security DB record.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security note says they're going with the Security DB record, implying the employee is actually a contractor.

Access policy:
1. full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system (Payroll Specialist for Payroll). Analyst doesn't own Payroll, so max would be write.
2. contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read.

The requested level is admin. The maximum is read (if contractor with basic training). So grant maximum = read.

The decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB lists E039 as contractor with basic security training, so max access is read (write only with advanced training, admin never). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant max = read.
